rationale: 601.2f is where cost reductions are applied when the total cost of the spell being cast is determined (the same process regardless of the zone it is cast from), and 118.7a states that a reduction of generic mana can only touch the generic component, so Grand Arbiter's {1} cannot eat the {U} or {R}.
The whole answer turns on Austere Command's modes being carried out in the order written during resolution, which 608.2c states, so the Bridge is already in the graveyard when the creature dies.

Bridge from Below's Zombie trigger is a leaves-the-battlefield trigger that looks back in time; 603.10a lists that class of trigger and 603.10 states the look-back principle, so the game sees Bridge on the battlefield rather than in the graveyard.

Three distinct steps: the destroyed token sits in the graveyard until the token-ceases-to-exist state-based action is checked (704.5d, with 704.3 giving the timing after resolution finishes); modes resolve in the order written (608.2c); and Bridge's intervening 'if' clause is rechecked on resolution (603.4), by which point the token is gone.

The count depends on the mentor triggers resolving last-on-first-off (405.2/405.5) and on what mentor actually does, which 702.134a defines as a +1/+1 counter on a target attacking creature with lesser power.

Convoke lets creatures be tapped as the spell's cost is paid (702.51a), that payment happens during casting (601.2h), and Emmara's tap trigger does not go on the stack until a player would next receive priority (603.3), so the token does not exist in time.
608.2h states that information a resolving ability needs from the game is determined once, when the effect is applied, so the empty graveyard at resolution sets the token count to zero.
106.7 defines what mana a permanent 'could produce'; since Nico's Exotic Orchard could produce nothing, no type can be defined for Abraham's.
106.7 defines the 'could produce' check that Star Compass makes, and 205.4c states that a land without the basic supertype is a nonbasic land even though Temple of Malady has basic land types.
106.7 is the rule the answer cites directly: the check assumes the ability resolving and ignores whether its costs or targets could be satisfied.
106.7 defines 'could produce' as any type a permanent's abilities would produce if they were to resolve, which covers both of Nykthos's abilities.
Phage's trigger is an intervening-'if' ability (603.4) whose 'you' means the controller of the permanent when it triggered, which 109.5 states is Nicholas, and he did not cast it from his hand.

The Quirion Ranger drawn and put back is a new object with no memory of its previous existence, stated either by 400.7 (it changed zones) or 401.6 (it stopped being revealed), so the granted ability's once-per-turn restriction is fresh.
401.6 states that a card played with from the top of the library that stops being revealed for any length of time becomes a new object, which is exactly what the Top shuffling does to Putrid Leech.

With an empty library Aspen only attempts a draw and would lose as a state-based action (121.4/704.5b, or 104.3c for being required to draw more than remain), and Platinum Angel's 'can't lose' overrides that per 101.2, so the turn continues with no card drawn or revealed.
702.95a spells out soulbond's two triggered abilities, each with an intervening 'if' requiring both creatures to be unpaired; Spectral Gateguards is already paired, so neither ability triggers.

The affected permanent's controller applies one replacement effect and then re-checks which effects now apply (616.1/616.1f), which is why Damping Sphere only becomes applicable after Mana Reflection doubles the mana, and 614.5 stops Mana Reflection from applying a second time.

605.1b establishes that Overgrowth's ability is a separate triggered mana ability, so the land itself is only tapped for one mana and Damping Sphere's 'tapped for two or more mana' condition is not met.
104.3c states directly that a player required to draw more cards than are left draws the remaining ones and then loses as a state-based action; 121.4/704.5b state the same loss condition.
The Goblin Arsonist is gone when its dies-trigger resolves, so the game uses its last known information; 608.2h and 113.7a each state that, and infect was part of that last known information.

Meng Huo's Horde is sacrificed while the activation cost is paid (601.2h, applied to abilities by 602.2b), so Sudden Spoiling never touches it, and the power Jarad uses is last known information per 608.2h/113.7a.

702.97a makes exiling the card part of scavenge's activation cost, 601.2h (applied to abilities by 602.2b) has that cost paid during activation, and 601.2i shows priority only comes back after the whole activation process is finished, so Nathalia cannot respond first.
Glacial Chasm's 'dealt to you' means its controller per 109.5, and 510.1b states the attacking creature's damage goes to the planeswalker it is attacking, not to Nico.

608.2j states an effect that refers to certain characteristics checks only those, so Treasure Vault also being a land does not matter to 'each artifact,' and 202.3a gives it mana value 0, inside Pernicious Deed's X=0 range.

702.19b is the trample damage-assignment rule and explicitly says that when checking for assigned lethal damage you do not take into account abilities or effects that might change the damage actually dealt, so protection is ignored and only 1 must go to Blightbeetle.

Personify exiles and returns Jeleva, so the permanent is a new object with no relation to the old one (400.7/403.4), and 607.2a is the linked-ability rule that ties 'cards exiled with Jeleva' only to cards exiled by that same object's ability.

704.3 states state-based actions are only checked when a player would next receive priority, i.e. after the equip ability finishes resolving, and 704.5f is the 0-toughness action that would have killed the Warrior if the Outfitter's bonus were not already applying.

702.51a defines convoke as a static ability functioning while the spell with convoke is on the stack and only for that spell's own total cost; 113.6d states such cost-modifying abilities function on the stack, so convoke does nothing for Disruption Aura's ability.

702.34a makes flashback an alternative cost applied through 601.2b and 601.2f-h, and 702.66a lets delve pay for generic mana in the spell's total cost after that total is worked out, so the two coexist.

607.2d links Sewer Nemesis's 'choose a player' ability to the abilities referring to the chosen player, and 607.5a states that when an object gains such an ability without a choice being made, the choice is undefined and that part of the ability does nothing.
607.2a is the linked-ability rule making Duplicant's second ability refer only to cards exiled by its own imprint ability, which is how it lands on the last of the two cards exiled.

205.1a states that setting an object's subtypes replaces the existing subtypes from that set, so Bludgeon Brawl's 'is an Equipment' strips Fortification, and 704.5n is the state-based action that unattaches an Equipment attached to an illegal permanent (the land).

701.3d states that an Aura leaving the battlefield counts as becoming unattached, and 702.103f states a bestowed Aura that becomes unattached stops being bestowed, which is why Noble Quarry comes back as a creature.

614.12 says replacement effects that modify how a permanent enters are worked out from the permanent's characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield, taking already-existing continuous effects such as Thalia's into account, and 614.12a states the devour choice is made before the permanent actually enters.
702.57b states a forecast ability may be activated only during the owner's upkeep step and only once each turn, so the extra upkeep from Paradox Haze does not allow a second activation.
Duplicant's non-characteristic-defining power/toughness-setting effect applies in layer 7b (613.4b), while +1/+1 counters are not applied until layer 7c (613.4c), so Skullbriar is seen as 1/1.

616.1 gives the affected permanent's controller the choice of which applicable replacement effect to apply first, which is why the count can be 11 or 12, and 614.5 states each effect gets only one opportunity.

119.7 states that when a player cannot gain life, a replacement effect that would replace a life gain event affecting that player does nothing; 614.7 states the same generally for replacing an event that never happens.

702.22c is the band-declaration rule: a band of this kind needs attacking creatures of the named quality plus one with 'bands with other [quality]', and neither the token nor the Sakashima copy satisfies both halves.

Phasing out sets the permanent's status and it phases back in before the controller's untap step (702.26b/702.26a); the Aura phases out and back in with it indirectly (702.26g); continuous effects on a phased-out permanent can expire while it is gone (702.26f); and 704.5m is the state-based check that lets Darksteel Mutation stay because it is attached to a creature.

702.26a gives the untap-step phase-out/phase-in timing, 702.26d states tokens keep existing while phased out and that no zone change occurs, and 702.26g/702.26h cover the attached permanents phasing out indirectly and returning still attached.

712.15a states a double-faced permanent cannot transform while face down, and 712.9/701.27c state that instructing a permanent that is not double-faced, such as Imagecrafter, to transform does nothing.

702.24a states that when a cumulative upkeep cost has choices, each choice is made separately per age counter and then the whole set is paid at once, and 810.9 states that in Two-Headed Giant life gain happens to each player individually before hitting the shared total, so both Vampires trigger.

603.8 is the state-trigger rule: it triggers as soon as the condition is met, goes on the stack at the next opportunity, and will not trigger again until it has left the stack. 608.2c has Living Death's steps happen in the order written, which is why the graveyard is momentarily empty.

113.6 states abilities of objects other than instants and sorceries normally function only on the battlefield, so protection is inactive in the graveyard; 701.3a/701.3b state an Aura cannot be attached to something it could not enchant and simply does not move; 704.5m/303.4c then put the unattached Aura into the graveyard as a state-based action.

201.2a states two objects have the same name if they share at least one name, which is what Spy Kit's extra names give Cloudseeder, and 111.1 states a token is a marker for a permanent not represented by a card, the distinction the answer draws between the token and the Cloud Sprite card.

616.1/616.1f have one Chains applied and then the process repeated for the second on the modified draw, 614.5 stops the first Chains from applying again to that same event, and 614.6 states the replaced draws never happen, so Sylvan Library sees no cards drawn with it.
614.6 states a replaced event never happens and the modified event occurs instead, which is why Sindbad's discard never happens and Keranos only triggers in the branches where a draw actually occurs.

Each Blightsteel Colossus has its own replacement effect turning its discard into a shuffle; 614.6 states the modified event occurs instead and may in turn trigger abilities, so two shuffles happen and Cosi's Trickster triggers twice.

614.12 states that to determine which replacement effects apply as a permanent enters, you check the permanent's characteristics as it would exist on the battlefield, where Dearly Departed would not be a Human.
